title: Electrical – Containment & Cabling
activity: Apartment electrical first fix – containment and cabling before close-up
status: Draft spot check from ITPs – for agreement

location.areaHint: e.g. Riser R2 L03 or Apartment 06.03.02

questions.q: Containment level and neat, brackets at max 1100 mm centres?
Conduits at the coordinated positions in the partitions, draw wires in every conduit?
Back boxes fitted level, at the set-out height, nothing missing?
Ask the fitter: What bracket centres are you working to, and is the dead test done? Could they answer?
questions.source: SuperPrime site practice – a fitter who can't answer is a red flag

questions.q: Cables on metal clips/bands at max ~300 mm horizontal / 400 mm vertical (no plastic-only fixings)?
questions.source: BS 7671 On-Site Guide typical clip spacing; Borough checklist

questions.q: Lighting and other drops coiled neatly in position above the ceiling, not lying loose?
Kitchen, bedroom (incl. wardrobe lights and blind boxes) and utility cupboard points all wired?
Controls cabling in: BMS/FCU, MVHR boost/humidistat, UFH floor sensors, KNX, blinds?
Data/TV, fibre and video entry (Cat6) cables in position and coiled?
Fire alarm first-fix cables in with fire-rated (metal) ties?
Main earth run to the mechanical cupboard; sub-main pulled to the electrical cupboard?
Dead test done before the walls and ceilings are closed?

notOk.t: Cables loose, not contained or protected at tray edges
Missing cable / containment IDs and labels
Trunking lids, end caps, saddles missing
Conduit flattened or cable sheath cut
Cables through knock-outs with no grommet

ask.q: What clip centres are you using on the cables?
ask.a: Metal clips/bands about 300 mm horizontal, 400 mm vertical – no plastic-only fixings.

ask.q: What bracket centres on the containment?
How are cables fixed in escape routes so they don't drop in a fire?
